Halvard.narrative: I keep Brandholm's palisade standing and set the work in the Carpenters' Yard; a wall is only as sound as the hands that mend it. I learned young that a full store and a locked door do not make a town righteous. My son made his home between the towns, and I will not pretend that makes him less mine.
goals: Keep the gates and palisade sound through the next hard season.
Teach Pell the work properly, not merely the motions.
See the Oath kept and the middle lands treated with respect.
Halvard.mood: Steady, with an old shame he rarely puts into words.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees what needs tending before I do, and usually says so.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: son
relations.note: He chose a difficult home, but I am proud he made it his own.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She has the patience to make a home across old divisions.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: I want him to learn a craft without having to choose a side.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She has a sturdy little way of asking why.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: I have held her only a few times, but she is ours.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: He listens closely; I must make sure he knows he belongs at the bench.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: former apprentice
relations.note: He learned the joints well and does not waste words.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I miss the man who used to laugh, and I do not press him.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She carries more than she lets the council see.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: A strong arm is no excuse to trample another household's work.

memories.gist: I was a young man in the Hunger Winter. We had timber and hides, and the shore families had children growing cold; I have never found a clean excuse for what we kept.
When Hekka and Sabeth's husband swore at the Stone, I stood close enough to hear every word. I hoped the promise would make the old hurt smaller.
Arne's first good gate brace held through a hard wind. I told him the joint was sound, and meant it as praise.
Pell arrived from Saltreach two years ago with more fishing sense than carpentry. He learned to set a straight line faster than I expected.
The last time Hakon brought the children to visit, Astrid kept finding one more thing to pack for them before they left.

stances.why: I have seen what happens when neighbors decide another family's hunger is not their concern.
I was there, and shame has lasted longer than the winter.
A wall protects everyone inside it, not just the hands that built it.
A straight joint holds; a loud claim does not.

Astrid.narrative: I keep berries, roots, and stores, and I notice when someone is hungry before they ask. Hakon lives at Oathstone with Rose and the children, so I miss him in the ordinary places: at the fire, by the door, in the work that used to need two pairs of hands. Pell is not my son, but he has had enough loss and distance; I mother him when he lets me.
goals: Keep enough berries and food stored for a hard winter.
Stay close to Hakon and his children, even when the walk between us feels long.
Make sure Pell has a warm place and people who ask after him.
Astrid.mood: Warm and busy, with a tender ache for the son who moved away.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He keeps the walls straight; I make sure he remembers to eat.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: son
relations.note: I miss his footsteps in the house, though I am glad he chose his own life.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She works hard and loves my son; I have no need to ask more.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He tries to act grown when he visits, and I feed him anyway.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She wants to know what every plant is called.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: A small warm bundle who makes me want to linger when it is time to go.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: apprentice
relations.note: I keep an eye on him; the boy has been away from his first home long enough.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is kind to Hakon and does not make a fuss about it.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: I worry that old woman has too few hands around her.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She works hard and remembers that trade keeps children warm.

memories.gist: When Hakon first left for Oathstone, I packed more berries than he could carry and pretended it was because they would spoil.
The first time I held Wynn, he had his father's serious brow and Rose's steady eyes. I wanted to keep him by the fire all day.
Pell came to Brandholm to learn from Halvard, and I found him hovering at the edge of the meal. I set him a place as if it had always been his.
Last berry season, Asa came back with stained fingers and a basket full of leaves. We sorted the good fruit together.

stances.why: A careful store is no use if the people under your roof are left cold or hungry.
Hakon, Rose, and their children are proof enough for me.
I have seen grown people argue while a child waited for food.
No one should have to earn a first bowl by explaining their whole life.

Pell.narrative: I was born in Saltreach, but I have lived in Brandholm for two years to learn carpentry from Halvard. I can mend a shelter and make a decent joint, though I still miss the sea and the sound of nets being worked. At the trade days, people ask me what one town thinks of the other as if I were a message-board with legs.
values: having room to make up my own mind
goals: Become a carpenter good enough that Halvard trusts me with serious work.
Keep in touch with Gwen, Robin, and Rook in Saltreach.
Be judged for my work instead of where I was born.
Pell.mood: Restless and watchful, but pleased when a piece of wood finally fits.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: master
relations.note: He corrects me plainly and gives me another chance to get it right.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother-figure
relations.note: She makes this house feel less like borrowed ground.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She raised me after my mother died; I miss her more than I say.

relations.name: Anselm
relations.label: uncle by marriage
relations.note: He has always made room for me without making a show of it.

relations.name: Robin
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He wants to know what the palisade looks like from inside.

relations.name: Rook
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She would climb the wall if I told her not to.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: We are family, though we have not had as much time together as I would like.

relations.name: Pim
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He asks about letters and the north, and I try to answer both.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: watchman
relations.note: He keeps asking what the hunters say, and I do not know what answer he wants.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He looks at me like a Saltreach boy has no business learning his father's trade.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: carpenter
relations.note: He is quieter than Halvard, but he has shown me a few tricks with a stubborn beam.

memories.gist: When I first came north two years ago, I had to learn which sounds were the palisade settling and which meant someone was at the gate.
Gwen gave me my first proper net-making knife and made me promise to keep it sharp. I still carry it when I can.
On one visit, Robin asked if Brandholm's palisade was as tall as the stories. I told him it was taller than he was.
Tobin stopped me at a trade day and questioned me about the hunters. I had little to tell him, but he watched my face as if I were hiding something.

stances.why: I have family and obligations on both sides of the stone.
The wood does not care how eager I am; a bad cut stays bad.
I can travel between my two homes because people agreed not to make every meeting a fight.
Tobin may have his reasons, but I cannot give him facts I do not have.
